quotes.text: Start facing the sled with the rope gripped firmly in both hands—one stacked over the other—arms slightly bent. Take a few steps back to create light tension in the rope.
quotes.closest: Start facing the sled with the rope gripped firmly in both hands—one stacked over the other—arms slightly bent. Take a few steps back to create light tension in the rope.

quotes.text: Plant your feet shoulder-width apart and lower into a quarter-squat, keeping your knees soft, chest up and core engaged. Your shoulders should stay over your hips, not leaning too far back.
quotes.closest: Plant your feet shoulder-width apart and lower into a quarter-squat, keeping your knees soft, chest up and core engaged. Your shoulders should stay over your hips, not leaning too far back.

quotes.text: To pull, step back one foot at a time, dragging the sled toward you. Each step should be short, quick, and controlled-think of driving through your midfoot while keeping the rope close to your body.
quotes.closest: To pull, step back one foot at a time, dragging the sled toward you. Each step should be short, quick, and controlled-think of driving through your midfoot while keeping the rope close to your body.

quotes.text: As the sled moves closer, feed the rope through your hands with small, continuous pulls; don't let slack build. Keep your elbows tucked in and your wrists firm to maintain control.
quotes.closest: As the sled moves closer, feed the rope through your hands with small, continuous pulls; don't let slack build. Keep your elbows tucked in and your wrists firm to maintain control.

quotes.text: As the rope piles up near your feet, flick or step it aside with small shuffles between steps to stop it tangling or tripping you.
quotes.closest: As the rope piles up near your feet, flick or step it aside with small shuffles between steps to stop it tangling or tripping you.

quotes.text: Keep your chin level and your gaze forward; looking down breaks posture and power.
quotes.closest: Keep your chin level and your gaze forward; looking down breaks posture and power.

quotes.text: Lead with your legs, not your arms. The rope is there for connection, not to “yank” the load.
quotes.closest: Lead with your legs, not your arms. The rope is there for connection, not to “yank” the load.

quotes.text: Focus on breathing: exhale with each backward step to maintain core pressure.
quotes.closest: Focus on breathing: exhale with each backward step to maintain core pressure.

quotes.text: It lights up your quads, glutes, and calves while still taxing your arms and back for stability.
quotes.closest: It lights up your quads, glutes, and calves while still taxing your arms and back for stability.

quotes.text: Backward sled drags are an effective conditioning tool to add to your training regime, as they provide higher quadriceps activation and metabolic demand than forward variations
quotes.closest: Backward sled drags are an effective conditioning tool to add to your training regime, as they provide higher quadriceps activation and metabolic demand than forward variations

quotes.text: When the pull becomes too heavy or your core gives way, it's easy to pitch your torso back and let your lower back take the load. But that robs your glutes, quads, and core of involvement - and puts your back at risk.
quotes.closest: When the pull becomes too heavy or your core gives way, it's easy to pitch your torso back and let your lower back take the load. But that robs your glutes, quads, and core of involvement - and puts your back at risk.

quotes.text: Stay anchored, keep your torso braced, and don't let your hips sag.
quotes.closest: Stay anchored, keep your torso braced, and don't let your hips sag.

quotes.text: The backward walk pull is energy-intensive and requires practice to coordinate the footwork with the rope pull. If your rope management slips, it's easy to lose rhythm or trip. Start with lighter loads and shorter distances before building toward race-day weights.
quotes.closest: The backward walk pull is energy-intensive and requires practice to coordinate the footwork with the rope pull. If your rope management slips, it's easy to lose rhythm or trip. Start with lighter loads and shorter distances before building toward race-day weights.

quotes.text: Under fatigue, people clench their core and stop breathing efficiently. That cuts your endurance. Keep a steady inhale/exhale rhythm tied to each pull or reset.
quotes.closest: Under fatigue, people clench their core and stop breathing efficiently. That cuts your endurance. Keep a steady inhale/exhale rhythm tied to each pull or reset.

quotes.text: If your form slips and your back rounds, it can place unnecessary strain on your lower spine, so it's important to keep your core tight and shoulders retracted throughout.
quotes.closest: If your form slips and your back rounds, it can place unnecessary strain on your lower spine, so it's important to keep your core tight and shoulders retracted throughout.
